message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a statutory holiday that falls on a weekday, creating a three‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Date(s) (2023) | Holiday (Observed) | Notes |
|----------------|--------------------|-------|
| **Jan 1 – 3** | New Year’s Day (observed Mon Jan 2) | Holiday fell on Sunday; observed on Monday. |
| **Feb 18 – 20** | Family Day (Alberta, BC, NB, NL, ON, PE, SK, MB) | Observed on Monday Feb 20. |
| **Apr 7 – 9** | Good Friday | Federal holiday; long weekend Fri‑Sun. |
| **May 20 – 22** | Victoria Day | Observed on Monday May 22. |
| **Jul 1 – 3** | Canada Day (observed Mon Jul 3) | Holiday fell on Saturday; observed on Monday. |
| **Sep 2 – 4** | Labour Day | Observed on Monday Sep 4. |
| **Oct 7 – 9** | Thanksgiving | Observed on Monday Oct 9. |
| **Nov 11 – 13** | Remembrance Day (observed Mon Nov 13) | Holiday fell on Saturday; observed on Monday. |
| **Dec 23 – 25** | Christmas Day | Observed on Monday Dec 25. |
| **Dec 24 – 26** | Boxing Day | Observed on Tuesday Dec 26. |

### Quick Tips for Your App

1. **Province‑specific holidays** – Family Day, Remembrance Day, and Boxing Day are not observed in every province. If you need province‑specific long weekends, add a filter for the relevant provinces.
2. **Observed dates** – When a holiday falls on a weekend, Canada observes it on the following Monday. Make sure your calendar logic accounts for this.
3. **Future planning** – For 2024, the pattern will shift slightly (e.g., Canada Day will be on Monday, so no extra day needed). Keep an eye on the “observed” dates each year.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province or if you need the data in a specific format (JSON, CSV, etc.).
